topBar.notice: Management system for Azura World Residence & Hotel. Demonstration with sample data.

hero.title: Azura World Residence & Hotel, run from one place.
hero.subtitle: 656 apartments, 7 blocks and 188 hotel rooms. Inventory, maintenance, accounting and documents in one system, with your own data.
hero.posterAlt: View of the Azura World Residence & Hotel development

why.title: What Azura World is
why.lead: A residential and hotel complex by {developer} in {district}. These are the key figures as the system holds them.

immersion.title: A day on site
immersion.lead: The same development across the day. Light, occupancy and operations change; the data behind them does not.
immersion.reducedMotionNotice: Motion is reduced. The view stays static.
immersion.noWebglNotice: The 3D view is unavailable on this device. A still image is shown.

amenities.title: The grounds
amenities.lead: Pools, aquapark and gardens on the site.

desire.title: The hotel on site
desire.lead: A five-star all-inclusive hotel inside the development, the difference from comparable projects in the region.

action.title: Request access
action.lead: Full access sits behind the sign-in. Accounts are reviewed and released by hand.

footer.rights: A demonstration for Azura World Residence & Hotel. All trademarks and image rights remain with their owners.

conflict.heading: Competing values
conflict.unresolvedNote: Deliberately unresolved. No average, no median, no “most likely” pick. Any single number here would be an invention with a citation stapled to it.

masterplan.title: Site plan
masterplan.schematicNote: A schematic of how the site is composed, not a floor plan. Select a block for details.
masterplan.blockNote: No source states how the apartments are split across the blocks. The split shown here is assumed to be even.

system.title: One record, many workflows
system.lead: Residents, management and accounting work in one system. Each role sees exactly what it needs.
system.demoNote: The units, blocks and hotel rooms are your own. The activity inside them is sample data: reports, entries and documents were created for this demonstration and are marked as sample data throughout the system.

residents.title: Residents and owners
residents.body: Their own apartment, contracts, payment status and house rules. A report takes two steps, with no phone call and no paperwork.
residents.detail: Owner, tenant and guest, plus sub-accounts for family members.

management.title: On-site management
management.body: Daily operations across all 7 blocks and 656 apartments. Who is responsible, what is open, what is due today.
management.detail: Site management, maintenance staff and outside contractors with their own access.

tickets.title: Reports and scheduling
tickets.body: From the fault to the sign-off in one track. Assignment, deadline, a reply to the person who reported it, and a history that still reads clearly later.
tickets.detail: Reports, work items, calendar and messages.

finance.title: Accounting and payments
finance.body: Service charges per block, payments, balances and contractor invoices. Amounts stay separated by currency and are never mixed.
finance.detail: Ledger, wallets and incoming invoices with approval.

documents.title: Documents and deadlines
documents.body: Contracts, minutes and certificates sit with the unit they belong to. Deadlines announce themselves before they pass.
documents.detail: Documents, inspections and reports ready to export.

admin.title: You run it yourself
admin.body: Add people, change roles, withdraw access. All of it without a developer, and every change is recorded with a name and a time.
admin.detail: Users, roles, settings and an audit trail you can export.

mediaKind.allRenders: Every frame in this section is a developer visualisation, not a photograph of the finished site.

flow.title: A system that runs alongside the whole day
flow.lead: Inventory, cases and records in one model. The numbers below are the scope the system holds today.
flow.flowLead: From the fault to the invoice in one track. Every step is logged and still reads clearly later.

report.title: Report
report.body: A resident reports in two steps, with no phone call and no paper.

assign.title: Assignment
assign.body: The technical team is assigned, with a deadline set by urgency.

work.title: In progress
work.body: The case runs with a reply to the reporter and photo evidence.

review.title: Sign-off
review.body: Resolved, checked and signed off with a name and a time.

settle.title: Settlement
settle.body: Costs land in the ledger, separated by currency, with approval.

workspace.caption: One workspace each role sees differently. The cases are sample data.

ledger.emptyHint: There are no entries for the filter you chose. Reset the filter to see everything.

immutable.heading: Posted entries cannot be changed
immutable.body: Once an entry is posted, the database blocks every change and every deletion. A wrong entry is not overwritten, it is cancelled with a matching reversal. That keeps what was originally recorded visible.
immutable.lockedReason: This entry is posted. Changes are blocked, corrections are made with a reversal.
immutable.voidReason: This draft was abandoned and is therefore closed.

balanceCheck.heading: Debit equals credit
balanceCheck.description: Every transaction must come to zero within each currency. Transactions that do not are listed here with their difference.
balanceCheck.singleSidedHint: A single entry with no counterpart is allowed, for example an accrual or an imported opening balance. It is not counted as an error here.
balanceCheck.empty: No grouped transactions in this view.

debtors.heading: Outstanding items
debtors.description: Posted charges less posted payments, per unit and per currency.

ageing.heading: Ageing
ageing.description: Open vendor invoices by how overdue they are, per currency. Measured against the server time, not your device clock.

reconciliation.heading: Payment matching
reconciliation.description: Payments that belong to no entry and no invoice are listed here. They are not hidden.
reconciliation.unmatchedHint: These payments arrived but are not assigned to an entry or an invoice.

reviews.intro: Each platform stands on its own, on its own scale.

platform.syndicatedNote: The same score is served by other sites as well. That is not a second, independent rating. It is the same number with a different logo in front of it.

A Booking.com-produced score does exist nonetheless: it was found as a badge on a third-party page, not on booking.com itself. That is why the platform card above names the site that served it.

modelled.body: No source published this apartment. We filled the inventory so the building is complete on screen. It is not a real offer and its price is not quoted anywhere.

realListing.body: This apartment appeared on a public property portal. The price and the size are exactly as that portal published them.

official.body: The developer or the hotel published this themselves.

sourceMissing.body: We looked for a source for this and did not find one.

notStated.body: Nobody publishes whether this apartment is free. We leave it open rather than guess.

confirmed.body: Two independent sources give the same figure.

conflicted.body: The sources give different figures. We show all of them instead of picking one.

singleSource.body: Only one source states this. It has not been checked against a second.

inferred.body: Worked out from other figures. It is not published anywhere in this form.

gap.body: No source states this. We leave it blank rather than estimate it.

sla.body: The time by which this job was promised to be done.

provenance.body: Where a figure came from: who published it, and when.

dataQuality.body: How well a figure is backed up: published by a source, or filled in by us.

available.body: A source lists this apartment as for sale.

reserved.body: Held for a buyer. Not sold yet.

priority.body: This sets where the job sits in the queue. Choose “Urgent” only for things like a flood or a safety risk that cannot wait. Picking a higher level does not make anyone arrive sooner — it only changes the order.
